V9's request, byte for byte, with prompt v1.6.0's system region in place of v1.5.0's, the prompt frozen and pushed at ed0ce1a before this packet existed; frozen and unapproved. An operator approval must cite this packet's id, version and digest, decide both disclosed risks, and live beside it.
approval_note: THIS DOCUMENT RECORDS NO APPROVAL. An approval lives beside it, in second-opportunity-synthesis-execution-approval-v10.json, names this packet's digest, and decides explicitly, for V10 only, both the residual semantic limitation and the strict first-request timeout risk, which 240 seconds reduces and does not remove. The V1 to V6 approvals and V9's are spent and name different digests: V9's was spent by its one request, whatever the answer was; V7 and V8 were superseded before execution and never had an approval, so none can be carried from them; and the TED egress decision permitted the material to leave, which is a different act from executing this model with this prompt at this cost
PROCESSING_PURPOSE: bounded external inference for Opportunity hypothesis synthesis
boundary_note: the Evidence and Claim ids of the selected packet, bound here so stage 7 reads the approved boundary from the digest-bound packet rather than from the object the gate was handed
PROVIDER_ROUTE: The Anthropic API, synchronous Messages endpoint, accessed with an API key under the Commercial Terms of Service. Not the Message Batches beta, and not a consumer subscription.
PROVIDER_SELECTION_BASIS: deterministic: exactly one provider route in the register currently satisfies every required property. gemini is NOT_APPROVED on its assessed unpaid route, which trains on submitted content; fake is NEVER_PRODUCTION by name. No preference, brand or capability judgement entered the choice
MODEL_SELECTION_BASIS: deterministic: exactly one text tier is configured in this deployment. LLM_TIER_FAST and LLM_TIER_BALANCED both bind provider 'null', which `TierBinding.configured` reads as unconfigured, and the embedding tier is local and forbidden here. There is no smaller approved model to prefer, and nothing was chosen for being strongest

adapter_default_note: a number this repository chose, which is neither a capability nor this packet's ceiling

estimate_note: Mission 1.84.5's count of schema v1.1.0's maximum instance as INPUT tokens. GENERATION_PARAMETERS.max_retries_note: 0, overriding the Gateway default of 2 and the deployment's LLM_MAX_RETRIES=2. A retry is a second call, and this packet authorises one
GENERATION_PARAMETERS.unsupported_parameters_note: null means the Gateway does not expose it, not that a default is accepted silently
GENERATION_PARAMETERS.response_schema_note: the tool carries the provider-strict projection; stage 5 validates the answer against the full output schema v1.2.0, which the projection is not

INPUT_PRICE_BASIS: 0.002 cost units per 1000 input tokens, from the deployment's configured pricing table
OUTPUT_PRICE_BASIS: 0.01 cost units per 1000 output tokens, from the same table
price_corroboration_note: the documented price, read again on 2026-09-14 (CI gate 94: D03 line 28, D08 lines 56 and 57), is 2 and 10 USD per million tokens and is now the standard price, the same figures as the held table
COST_UNIT_NOTE: cost units are provider-agnostic by ADR-006: a unit is whatever the configured table's author intended. The ceiling is expressed in the same units the budget ledger compares and subtracts, so it is enforceable without this record asserting a currency

TIMEOUT.TIMEOUT_BASIS: the operator's availability budget, decided in Mission 1.84.21 and recorded by CI gate 96: a client-side budget beyond the documented 180-second provider grammar compilation timeout, with additional operational margin. It replaces the reviewed 60 seconds V1 to V8 carried, and the deployment's LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, which this path does not read

documentation.verbatim: long-running requests that can hit system timeouts and open-connection limits
documentation.scope: said of thinking budgets above 32k; it establishes that a long request can hit a timeout, and no rate

TIMEOUT.note: The operator selected 128000 output tokens and a 240-second client timeout. The transport is not streamed, so the timeout covers the wait for the whole answer, and nothing held documents how many tokens a synchronous request produces in that time. The client now waits longer than the provider's documented 180-second grammar compilation limit, so the mismatch V8 carried is reduced; compilation and generation together are not bounded by anything documented, so V10's one request may still end at the timeout, fail-closed with no retry. No end-to-end latency bound is established, and the risk is the operator's to accept or refuse
TIMEOUT.compilation_basis: CI gate 94's reading of the structured-outputs page (D04): a grammar compiled on the first request with a schema, cached for 24 hours from last use, and a compilation timeout of 180 seconds; the latency of a first compilation is not documented. CI gate 96 carries the fragments
TIMEOUT.CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MECHANISM: the value travels unchanged from the request to urllib.request.urlopen(timeout=...), a socket timeout on the blocking operations of one non-streamed request. The gateway applies no ceiling of its own, and the deployment's LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is not read on this path

PROVIDER_COMPLETION_POLICY.precedence_note: The signal is read from the response the runner retained, at stage 3, before the structured output is parsed, validated or judged. A response cut at the limit can carry a parseable object, every required key, even an object the whole v1.1.0 schema accepts, and none of it is consulted: stages 4 to 10 are recorded NOT_REACHED. There is no second request, no continuation and no repair

documentation.verbatim: Claude responds with `stop_reason: "tool_use"` and one or more `tool_use` blocks.
The output may be incomplete and not match your schema
If generation then reaches the context window limit, it stops with `stop_reason: "model_context_window_exceeded"`.

STAGE_CONDITIONS.6_semantic_output_gate_v1_4_0: gate v1.4.0 over the answer as it arrived, with the trusted context and the registry's source-metadata channel; gate v1.3.0 called once, its structural reasons read against schema v1.2.0; fixed in the runner and never injectable
STAGE_CONDITIONS.7_evidence_boundary_and_no_distortion: every cited Evidence and Claim id inside the approved boundary this packet binds, each Evidence cited with its approved Claim, and the v1.4.0 audit gate v1.4.0 returns, which is gate v1.3.0's own, with no failed field
STAGE_CONDITIONS.8_attribution_and_provenance: every provenance field the first revision must carry is present, the request id read by its header name
STAGE_CONDITIONS.9_persistence_eligibility: the canonical OpportunityHypothesis (opportunity-hypothesis@1.0.0) constructs from the answer in memory; nothing is persisted, and an answer it refuses is not eligible for review
STAGE_CONDITIONS.10_human_review: REQUIRED_NOT_PERFORMED: no machine stage stands in for the human review

validation_note: the ten ordered stages, V6's exactly. The first that fails decides and no later stage runs. Stage 5 is the full schema v1.2.0 validator, never the strict projection; stage 6 is gate v1.4.0 and cannot be injected; stage 7 reads the approved boundary from this packet; stage 9 constructs the canonical OpportunityHypothesis in memory; stage 10 is a human. Strict decoding is not a stage

provenance_the_first_revision_must_carry: the semantic gate version and its implementation digest
the generation-headroom policy and its record
the reasoning-summary contract decision and its record
the gate v1.4.0 freeze record and its commit
the output capacity analysis under schema v1.2.0
the provider-strict projection record and its freeze commit
the prompt v1.6.0 record and its freeze commit
PERSISTENCE_POLICY.note: an answer that passes every machine stage is eligible for human review and nothing more; persisting it needs a separate operator approval

structured_output_note: the output mechanism is FORCED_STRICT_TOOL_USE: tool_choice still forces the one synthesis tool, and the tool definition carries strict: true at its top level, beside its name, description and input schema, with no beta header. Strict decoding is what the provider does while generating; it is not a validation stage, and PROVIDER_STRICT_SUBSET_COMPLIANCE is not FULL_CANONICAL_SCHEMA_COMPLIANCE, which remains LOCAL_STAGE_5_ONLY. The provider documents that a refusal or a max_tokens stop may not match the schema, and stage 3 reads the stop reason before any parse
tools_note: the forced structured-output tool is the reviewed output mechanism and not a capability: it executes nothing. Making it strict changes how the provider decodes its input, not what it can do

RETENTION_ON_EXECUTION.raw_provider_response: RETAINED on every path where a response arrived, including an output-limit stop: the body itself, redacted, with hidden reasoning stripped
RETENTION_ON_EXECUTION.parsed_structured_output: RETAINED where a tool input exists, with whether any stage judged it
RETENTION_ON_EXECUTION.usage_metadata: RETAINED from the Gateway's telemetry and from the response's own usage block
RETENTION_ON_EXECUTION.hidden_reasoning: NOT RETAINED, and not requested. Thinking is disabled, and a reasoning block volunteered anyway is stripped at any depth

PREPARATION_VERIFICATION.$comment: what verification found on the preparing machine, from the research database, the runner's own verify() with every network path tripwired and nothing set aside. CI cannot rebuild these and checks them for agreement with the approved digests instead

preparation_accounting.$comment: what PREPARING this packet did, which is a different fact from what executing it would do. No documentation page was requested: the provider facts are those CI gate 94 holds. Excluded from the digest

digest_covers: everything V9's digest bound except V9's risk flags and V6's schema violation; with V10's identity, prompt v1.6.0's version, digest and record, the generation-surface policy, its renderer and its block digest, the prompt freeze commit, V9 as the consumed predecessor with its outcome, failed stage, execution record digest and refusal families, V8 and V7 as superseded, the seven consumed packets, the request body's digest and length, the planning figures recomputed over it, gate 94's hard ceiling and record digest, the 240-second timeout, and both risk flags V10 does not carry. It excludes itself, the preparation date, the notes, the TIMEOUT block's commentary, V9's reconfirmation, the freeze push record, the synthetic preflight, what verification found and the accounting, so an approval recorded later cannot move it
headroom_note: each of the twelve composed texts is stated with a generation target, floor(hard maximum x 4/5), beside its hard maximum, now read from schema v1.2.0: the reasoning summary's row moves to 1200 and 1500, and no other row moves. A target is guidance for writing; the validator, the gate and the persistence model do not know it exists
contract_note: the contract is V6's, unchanged: output schema v1.2.0, whose reasoning summary has a hard maximum of 1500 and a generation target of 1200. Stage 5 validates the answer against it, locally and in full, whatever the tool schema carried
strict_note: V10 sends V9's request with prompt v1.6.0's system region: the forced tool is strict, and its input schema is the provider-strict projection of schema v1.2.0, frozen by CI gate 92 and pushed as 57154af. The projection keeps every property name, every required list, every type and enum, the uuid format, and every object closed with additionalProperties false; it sends none of the 30 constraints it classifies LOCAL_ONLY, and each of those is still enforced by the full schema at local stage 5

PLANNING_ESTIMATION_BASIS.measured_pair: Mission 1.31.1's provider response reported 5967 input tokens for the docker prompt. That prompt was re-rendered here at 12868 wire characters, giving 2.1565 characters per token
PLANNING_ESTIMATION_BASIS.wire_definition: len(json.dumps(body)): the request body exactly as the transport serialises it, built locally by the adapter with this packet's parameters and never sent
PLANNING_ESTIMATION_BASIS.limitation: a ratio measured on one prompt and applied to another, over characters rather than tokens. The provider's count endpoint would measure it, and no request of any kind is made in this mission
PLANNING_ESTIMATION_BASIS.note: the body-based figure, recomputed over V10's own serialised body by gate 94's derivation: an engineering estimate, never a bound. The multiplier's margin covers the documented tool-use prompt; nothing covers the strict-format prompt, whose size is not documented, and the hard ceiling does not use this figure

cost_note: The hard execution ceiling is gate 94's and V9's, 3.608, resting on documented bounds only: at most 1000000 billable input tokens, the model's context window, which holds every input the provider adds; 128000 output tokens; and the 1.1 data-residency multiplier, because the request leaves inference_geo to a workspace default this repository cannot see. The planning estimate is recomputed from V10's 34261-character body, the body-based input estimate plus all 128000 output tokens at the held price: a planning figure, never a bound. V9's observed usage enters neither figure

OBSERVED_USAGE_NOT_USED.note: V9 used 12493 input and 3734 output tokens: one observation, which bounds nothing about the next call and enters neither figure

supersession_note: V9 was executed once and spent; V8 was superseded before execution for CLIENT_TIMEOUT_SHORTER_THAN_PROVIDER_STRICT_COMPILATION_TIMEOUT, and V7 before it for COST_CEILING_SEMANTICS_NOT_PROVEN. None of them is edited, and none can be executed again. V10 is V9 with prompt v1.6.0 and nothing else, and its body is V9's bytes with the v1.6.0 system region
risk_note: the approval must decide two risks, each explicitly and for V10 only. The residual semantic limitation of the vocabulary-bounded gate v1.4.0; and an availability risk: whether the strict grammar V9 compiled is still cached is not established, and no end-to-end latency bound is established, so V10's only call, with no retry, may end at the 240-second timeout before an answer arrives. Neither is accepted here, and an approval that does not accept both executes nothing
timeout_note: The client timeout is V9's, the operator's 240 seconds, an availability budget: not a provider guarantee, not a latency prediction, not a statistical estimate and not a billing bound. V9's one request answered in 54.6 seconds, one observation that establishes nothing about the next, and did not move the timeout. The timeout is passed to the transport and is no part of the provider body
